'''Marion Elizabeth Stark''' (23 Aug 1894<ref>Biographic data at WorldCat {{oclc|5894492657}}</ref> &ndash; 15 April 1982)<ref>{{cite web | publisher=The University of Chicago Library | series=Campus Publications | title=Deaths|work=University of Chicago Magazine | volume=75 | issue=1 | date=Sep 1982 |page=45| url=http://campub.lib.uchicago.edu/view/?docId=mvol-0002-0075-0001#page/52/mode/1up|editor-first=Felicia Antonelli|editor-last= Holton}}</ref> was an American mathematician. She was one of the first women to receive a [[Ph.D.]] in mathematics.<ref name="Green.LaDuke.2008">{{cite book | title-link= Pioneering Women in American Mathematics | isbn=978-0-8218-4376-5 | first1 = Judy | last1 = Green | author1-link = Judy Green (mathematician) | first2 = Jeanne | last2 = LaDuke | author2-link = Jeanne LaDuke | title=Pioneering Women in American Mathematics &mdash; The Pre-1940 PhD's | publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]], The [[London Mathematical Society]] | series=History of Mathematics | volume=34 | edition=1st | date=2008 }} Biography on pp.&nbsp;575–577 of the [https://www.ams.org/bookpages/hmath-34-PioneeringWomen.pdf Supplementary Material] at [https://www.ams.org/publications/authors/books/postpub/hmath-34 AMS]</ref>

==Education and career==
She got her [[A.B.]] in 1916, and her [[Master of Arts|A.M.]] in 1917, both from [[Brown University]].<ref name="ChicagoUniversityRecord.1924"/> In 1917, she became the professor of mathematics [[Meredith College]] in [[Raleigh, North Carolina]]. In autumn 1919, she started teaching in [[Wellesley College]] as a part-time instructor, while attending courses of [[Helen Abbot Merrill]] and [[Mabel M. Young]].<ref>{{cite web | title=The Wellesley News (09-25-1919) | publisher=Wellesley College | date=Sep 1919 | url=https://repository.wellesley.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1603&context=news | access-date=2017-11-08 | archive-date=2017-11-09 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171109080933/https://repository.wellesley.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1603&context=news | url-status=dead }} p.&nbsp;6; with typos in middle initial and academic degree</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=The Wellesley Legenda 1920 | publisher=Wellesley College | year=1920 | url=https://repository.wellesley.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1030&context=legenda | access-date=2017-11-08 | archive-date=2017-11-09 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171109023618/https://repository.wellesley.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1030&context=legenda | url-status=dead }} p.&nbsp;26</ref> In the 1923 summer quarter, and, supported by a fellowship, in autumn 1924 through summer 1925, she studied at the [[University of Chicago]]<ref name="ChicagoUniversityRecord.1924">{{cite web | publisher=The University of Chicago Library | series=Campus Publications | title=University Record (New Series) | volume=10 | issue=3 | date=Jul 1924 | url=http://campub.lib.uchicago.edu/view/?docId=mvol-0445-0010-0003#page/65/mode/1up}}</ref> where she received her Ph.D. in 1926.<ref name="Green.LaDuke.2008"/><ref>{{cite thesis | type=Ph.D. thesis | author=Marion Elizabeth Stark | title=A Self-Adjoint Boundary value Problem Associated with a Problem of the Calculus of Variations | institution=University of Chicago | year=1926 | oclc=213821 }}</ref><ref>{{mathGenealogy|6115}}</ref>

In 1927, she was appointed assistant professor of mathematics at Wellesley,<ref>{{cite journal | title=Notes | journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society | volume=33 | issue=6 | date=Nov–Dec 1927 | page=798 | url=https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.bams/1183492328}}</ref><ref>{{cite book | title=Legenda 1928 | year=1928 | publisher=Wellesley College | url=https://archive.org/details/wellesleylegenda1928bost}}. [https://archive.org/stream/wellesleylegenda1928bost#page/22/mode/2up p.&nbsp;23]</ref> in 1936, she was promoted to an associate professor there.<ref>{{cite web | publisher=The University of Chicago Library | series=Campus Publications | title=University of Chicago Magazine | volume=29 | issue=1 | date=Nov 1936 | url=http://campub.lib.uchicago.edu/view/?docId=mvol-0002-0029-0001#page/48/mode/1up}}</ref> In 1945, she was promoted to a professorship;<ref>{{cite journal | title=Notes | journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society | volume=51 | issue=7 | date=Jul 1945 | page=515 | url=https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.bams/1183507126}}</ref> in 1946, she became Chairman of the Department.<ref>{{cite web | publisher=The University of Chicago Library | series=Campus Publications | title=University of Chicago Magazine | volume=39 | issue=3 | date=Dec 1946 | url=http://campub.lib.uchicago.edu/view/?docId=mvol-0002-0039-0003#page/27/mode/1up}}</ref> In 1960, she retired from Wellesley after 40 years, her last rank being a Lewis Atterbury Stimson Professor of Mathematics.<ref name="Green.LaDuke.2008"/><ref>{{cite web | title=Report of the President 1958–1960 | publisher=Wellesley College | url=https://repository.wellesley.edu/do/search/?q=marion%20stark%20retire&start=0&context=1912413&facet=publication_year%3A1961 | access-date=2017-11-08 | archive-date=2017-11-09 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171109023445/https://repository.wellesley.edu/do/search/?q=marion%20stark%20retire&start=0&context=1912413&facet=publication_year:1961 | url-status=dead }} p.&nbsp;20</ref>

==Recognition==
Stark was named a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 1938.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/historic|title=Historic Fellows|publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science|access-date=2021-04-20}}</ref>
